title: Zero resistance: transport evidence and its limits
summary: What a zero-resistance measurement establishes, which controls it needs, and why transport alone does not establish bulk superconductivity.

Replace that attribution with Halperin and Nelson (1979), DOI 10.1007/BF00116988, and classify the supported statement as theory. The earlier paper is related vortex-dynamics background, not the cited superconducting-film treatment.

claims.statement: A reported zero resistance is an operational result: the voltage is below the detection threshold for a specified current and contact geometry. The experiment establishes a bound on resistance rather than a mathematical proof that it is exactly zero. This article concerns electrical transport; magnetic expulsion and thermodynamic anomalies require separate measurements. The superconducting condensate provides the theoretical setting, but a microscopic model does not replace the experimental controls.
claims.conditions: DC four-probe transport; retain current, geometry, voltage threshold, magnetic field, sample and observation time. Equilibrium and driven optical responses are separate.
claims.verificationScope: See each source verification label; this ledger does not certify primary findings.

claims.statement: Record resistance onset, midpoint and zero separately. An onset can identify a small superconducting region, whereas a connected path may determine the zero-resistance result. Neither number alone measures the superconducting volume fraction. Filaments, an interface or a second phase can dominate a four-terminal path even when most of the specimen remains normal. This distinction is central when comparing bulk crystals, films and high-pressure samples.

claims.statement: This expression is a measurement definition, not a universal material law. It assumes a meaningful current path, stable contacts and a noise floor evaluated under the actual acquisition conditions. In a homogeneous specimen, converting resistance to resistivity further requires the sample dimensions. The ideal condensate response is a limiting statement about frequency, temperature, field and current; a finite experiment cannot take every limit simultaneously.

claims.statement: Halperin and Nelson developed a vortex-unbinding description of resistive behavior in dirty superconducting films, including fluctuation conductivity above an effective vortex-unbinding temperature and nonlinear resistivity below it. This is a theoretical treatment of a specified film regime, not a measurement of pairing symmetry. When applying it to data, this article requires independent checks of the model assumptions and sample conditions; a fit alone is not treated as a unique diagnosis. The publisher abstract supports this limited description; its full derivation has not yet been reviewed here.
claims.conditions: Dirty two-dimensional superconducting films in the vortex-unbinding treatment; effective transition and fluctuation regime. Applying a fit requires sample-specific assumptions; no pairing-symmetry inference.
claims.verificationScope: Publisher abstract of Halperin and Nelson (1979), DOI 10.1007/BF00116988, checked 2026-10-18. Full derivation not accessed; diagnostic requirements are editorial guidance.

claims.statement: Light-driven optical signatures must remain in a different evidence category from an equilibrium transport transition. Mitrano and colleagues reported a transient superconducting-like response in driven K3C60. The source chapter itself retains the ambiguity of assigning superconductivity from optics alone. Budden and colleagues investigated a longer-lived driven state with transport observations; those observations do not define an equilibrium zero-resistance critical temperature. This pilot does not promote either optical scale into a bulk temperature ranking.

claims.statement: A persistent current can be complementary evidence, but its interpretation needs the loop geometry and decay time. A single low-resistance reading cannot supply those quantities. Likewise, magnetic-field suppression supports a superconducting interpretation without uniquely identifying the pairing interaction.

claims.statement: Treat zero resistance as one part of an evidence chain. A useful candidate report specifies a measurable threshold, demonstrates repeatability and connects transport to other probes. Preserve negative controls and the possibility of a minority superconducting path. This approach makes a discovery claim more testable while keeping unresolved volume fraction, phase identity and mechanism explicitly open.
